feature: QRNG-RECOVERY-01 / F-01 activation self-check batch scope
defect: 2.58.217 delta review F-01 (non-blocking): services/mca_random_source.py::_confirm_activation reserved a chunk without exact batch scope, so an older LfDR/NULL-fingerprint batch could satisfy the activation self-check while mca_random_state.activation_batch_id named the newly fetched ANU batch (wrong provenance, no false hardware-quantum claim).

environment.network: none; ANU HTTP is injected via mrs._HttpResponse; temp SQLite per test; no production access
environment.config: test fixtures only (_hot_setting/_read_memory_setting fakes); no environment gate or factory default changed

change.store_api: RandomStore.reserve_chunk(k, *, config_fingerprint=None, provider_ids=None, batch_id=None) — additive optional exact-batch predicate; None preserves the existing oldest-first selection for all existing callers (dream chunk, tests). Empty/unknown batch_id yields an empty SQL predicate (AND 0), never an unscoped fallback.
change.activation: RandomSourceService._confirm_activation(batch_id) passes batch_id to reserve_chunk and refuses a chunk whose batch_id differs from the requested one (contract guard). Journal provider/batch_id come from the consumed item; mca_random_state.activation_batch_id is written only after that item is consumed, so state names the batch actually consumed.
change.no_fallback: If the target batch has no consumable value, _confirm_activation returns False: no foreign value is consumed, no journal row and no activation state are written; activate() reports validation_failed with deposited=false.

covers: store exact scope + empty/unknown safety + legacy order

failure_reasons: mixed batch: ANU batch reserved_upto/consumed_upto stayed (0,0) while the older LfDR batch was consumed
_confirm_activation returned True using the older LfDR batch (false activation confirmation)
RandomStore.reserve_chunk() has no batch_id keyword on base (TypeError)

items.seam: exact batch scope removed in reserve_chunk
silent fallback to unscoped reserve when the target batch is empty
original defect + forced journal attribution (scope removed, guard removed, journal names the requested batch)

no_regression_evidence.existing_activation_test: tests/test_mca10a_random_source_block_b_round1037.py::test_activation_real_batch_quantum_activated passed both on base (single batch) and candidate (part of the 314 batch)
no_regression_evidence.store_callers: the only other reserve_chunk caller (dream chunk, services/mca_random_source.py:3589) passes no batch_id and keeps oldest-first selection

limitations: The negative (no consumable value in the target batch) case calls _confirm_activation directly: no public path can leave a freshly inserted batch exhausted without a crash between insert and self-check; the direct seam is the same production code that activate()/_do_refill call.
No production access and no real ANU request were made; provider responses are injected. This is a provenance/scope fix, not a statistical randomness change.
A crash after reserve_chunk but before journal flush can still lose the reserved value (pre-existing watermark contract); the fix does not change that behavior.
reviewer_questions: Is the additive batch_id predicate on RandomStore.reserve_chunk (default None) acceptable as the minimal shared-mechanism fix, versus adding provider_ids to the activation self-check?
Is the contract guard (consumed item batch_id must equal the requested batch) considered part of the required invariant or redundant defense?
Is the direct _confirm_activation negative test acceptable, given the public activation path always inserts a fresh consumable batch?
release: no bump, no deploy, no production access; product commit 00d9ce3f8 expects independent review before integration
